summary: Staged _exeque meets completion-bar items 1-5: the only out-of-default construct, volatile GpuCtx.unk08, is exactly the field-level scope admitted by landed owner ruling Q95 (9d67f1aa7); the single do-while(0) is FAKE-labelled with a reason I re-measured (10/187 without it); prototypes, the cast and the comments are truthful; the _que aliases are retired in favour of the header aggregate.

evidence.explanation: Q95 is landed in a blocking catalog file (.claude/rules/legitimate-volatile-interrupt-touched.md:34-38, commit 9d67f1aa7; verbatim owner record in docs/grind/owner-rulings-2026-09-26.md batch 44). The diff qualifies this one field only. No other GpuCtx member or other object becomes volatile, and the precheck shows new_extern_volatile = []. The grounds hold: DMACallback(2, _exeque) is at src/display.c:948, and the target has sw $zero,0($v1); jalr $v0; nop at 0x8007D988-D990 (asm/funcs/_exeque.s:179-181). The only asm consumers of 0x8009BE7C are _addque2 (0x8007D480, sw 1) and _exeque. That matches the allowlist row.

evidence.construct: do { D_8009BF70 = _que[_qout].count; } while (0); with /* FAKE: ... score 10 ... */
evidence.explanation: This is pre-cleared shape 7 (no-new-park-categories), labelled at the site with a measured reason. I ablated it myself (tmp/_exeque/rv_q95/nowrap.c): sandbox --disable all = 10/187 (186 insns). So it is load-bearing and the stated score is accurate. The worker's 105-variant placement sweep ([s13]) found that only this single wrap reaches 0. No spelling with fewer FAKEs is known in the ledger or rejected/.

The header declares drawsync_cb as u32. DrawSyncCallback (src/display.c:45-46) stores the user's callback there, so calling it through a function-pointer cast is truthful. It uses the existing GpuCtx member, with no second handle.

evidence.construct: s32 _exeque(); forward decls (display.c:907, 1043) and the s32 _exeque(void) definition
evidence.explanation: The function returns (_qin - _qout) & 0x3F, the queue depth (asm tail 0x8007D9A8-D9AC), and 1 on the DMA-busy early-out. s32 is truthful. The old void decl was the false one, and the new type is compatible with DMACallback's s32 (*)().

This is the saved interrupt mask (sw at 0x8007D71C after SetIntrMask(0), reloaded at 0x8007D914 for the restore). It mirrors D_8009BF80 in _addque2 and D_8009BF88 in _reset. No header or named_syms entry already declares 0x8009BF84, and asm/data/7D920.data.s defines it, so this is not a second handle.

evidence.construct: _que[_qout].func/.arg/.count via extern volatile GpuQueueItem _que[64]; removal of _que_plus_0x4/0x8/0xC
evidence.explanation: The body reaches the queue only through the existing header aggregate (include/gpu.h:134-141), with no per-word alias. The removed aliases are now referenced only by asm/funcs/_addque2.s, asm/funcs/_exeque.s and asm/text2.s. None of those is linked: bb2.ld names no text2.o, and LINKED_ASM_FUNCS is empty. So the removal is link-safe.

I re-ran sandbox _exeque --disable all on the staged tree: 0/187. build/bb2.exe was rebuilt at 11:04:18, after every staged build input (11:02:51), and has SHA1 62efab4f73f992798c43e8c730aa43baa10bb4fa == oracle. The only objects older than gpu.h are orphans with no src/*.c. I did not run verify-oracle --rebuild myself because it refuses on the dirty tree and the reviewer stays read-only.
There is no asm, pin, barrier, rule/config, Makefile, linker or pipeline change in the diff (git diff --cached; precheck: 0 rules, 0 pins, 0 asm blocks, 0 hardcoded $N).

hygiene_debt: The commit body has no 'IRQ writer:' line. Suggest adding 'IRQ writer: _exeque():src/display.c:969 — installed via DMACallback(2, _exeque) at src/display.c:948' and 'Use-site construct: test-then-clear (Q95 field waiver)' per legitimate-volatile-interrupt-touched.md Procedure step 3. The allowlist row also cites addresses rather than file:line.

Stale comments after alias retirement: include/gpu.h:129-131 ('the +4/+8/+C rows stay in the symbol config as aliases until _exeque leaves INCLUDE_ASM'), undefined_syms_auto.txt _que row ('per-word aliases below retire with _exeque'; none remain), src/display.c:922-923 (names D_80103680[64]; the object is _que).
GpuCtx.drawsync_cb is typed u32 rather than a function pointer, which forces the call-site cast. Retyping it is a header cleanup across DrawSyncCallback/_addque2/_exeque.
named_syms.txt:1171 names 0x8009BF80 g_gpu_motion_save_a ('motion_make_table state'), but _addque2 uses it as the saved interrupt mask (D_8009BF80, pre-existing; outside this function).
